## CPython 3.13 Free Threading and Extension Imports

CPython 3.13 introduced free threading as an experimental configuration in which the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) can be disabled. In this mode, an application’s runtime choice meets a separate compatibility question when it imports an extension.

If an extension has no explicit declaration of support for free threading, importing it produces a warning and enables the GIL. The way an extension makes that declaration differs between multi-phase and single-phase initialization.

Declaring support signals compatibility with the free-threaded runtime; it does not mean the extension’s code is thread-safe. Those are separate responsibilities for extension authors.
